commands.author: yetval

target.title: Proposal: reproduce and attest real behavior proof instead of only reading it
target.body:
### This is something I would like to work/collaborate on please dont open a PR for this! ## TL;DR - ClawSweeper judges whether a PR's "real behavior proof" is sufficient by having a model **read** the pasted evidence. The resulting `proof: sufficient` label is then trusted by its duplicate/superseded-**close** safety checks. It never re-runs the proof (`grep -rn "attest" src/` = 0). - This adds a bounded lane that **reproduces** proof for the reproducible subset: run the declared reproduction on base vs head in a network-denied, no-credential sandbox, require a behavior delta, and write a head-pinned **attestation** the close check can prefer over the model's label, behind a default-off flag. - Deterministic and fail-closed, staged so the mutation-free reproduce-and-attest lands first and the sandbox plus the label-trusting change get explicit maintainer review. ## Summary ClawSweeper's "real behavior proof" is a single model judgment. A Codex review, granted live network to fetch attacker-controlled PR body, links, screenshots, and video (`clawsweeper.ts:7326`), emits a `RealBehaviorProof` object (`clawsweeper.ts:426`). Deterministic code then turns `status === "sufficient"` into the `proof: sufficient` label (`clawsweeper.ts:11130`). That label, plus the model's report status, is what the proof-nudge lanes and the duplicate/superseded-close safety checks trust: `proofPassedInLabels` inside the covering-close safety check (`apply-result.ts:1104`) and its canonical-close sibling `unsafeCanonicalPullRequestReason` (`clawsweeper.ts:13612`). ClawSweeper never re-runs the declared reproduction (`grep -rn "attest" src/` = 0). Scope this precisely: the automerge gate does not read a proof regex; it gates on checks plus exact-head trusted ClawSweeper review readiness (`automerge-shepherd.ts:42-82`). So the trust a reproduction lane displaces is the proof label and the close-safety checks, not the merge decision itself. This proposes a bounded Proof Reproduction and Attestation lane: for the narrow subset where a reproduction is actually declared and offline-deterministic, ClawSweeper checks out base and head in a network-denied, de-privileged, no-credential sandbox, runs the reproduction, captures exit codes and output hashes, requires a behavior delta (old on base, new on head), and writes a head-SHA-pinned attestation next to the model verdict. A valid attestation can then be preferred over the model-derived label at `apply-result.ts:1104`, behind a default-off flag. It is staged so the mutation-free parts land first and the label-trusting change stays maintainer-gated. _How proof is trusted today, and where it breaks:_ ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Contributor writes proof claim in PR body"] --> B["Codex review reads PR body, links, media
(live network granted, clawsweeper.ts:7326)"] B --> C["Model emits RealBehaviorProof
status and evidenceKind only, no command, no SHA, no hash
(clawsweeper.ts:426)"] C --> D["Deterministic: status sufficient becomes label proof: sufficient
(clawsweeper.ts:11130)"] D --> E{"Close-safety checks trust the label/report
proofPassedInLabels (apply-result.ts:1104)
unsafeCanonicalPullRequestReason (clawsweeper.ts:13612)"} E -->|"label or report matches"| F["Admit duplicate / superseded / canonical CLOSE"] B -. "BREAK: attacker-controlled media can steer the judgment; reproduction is never re-run (attest = 0)" .-> C E -. "BREAK: close-safety trusts a model-derived label, no reproduction, no head SHA, no hash" .-> F ``` > **Update (2026-07-05):** Re-verified against `main` after #424 ("keep Mantis focused on QA proof"). The core chain is unchanged: proof is still a model read (`RealBehaviorProof`), the `proof: sufficient` label is still derived from `status`, and the close-safety anchor `apply-result.ts:1104` is byte-identical. #424 narrows Mantis to **proof-only** (reproduce or inspect Telegram/Discord/web-UI-chat surfaces and return redacted evidence, never mutate GitHub state) and drops the `slack_desktop_smoke`/`visual_task` schema arms in favor of `web_ui_chat_proof`, the same reproduce-and-inspect philosophy this proposal extends into deterministic, close-safety-grade reproduction. Symbol names below are authoritative; `clawsweeper.ts` line numbers are pinned to the filing SHA and have since drifted by roughly +1 to +90 (e.g. the label-sync helper `nextRealBehaviorProofSufficientLabels` is now near `:11216`, the canonical-close helper `unsafeCanonicalPullRequestReason` near `:13706`).
Full proposal (background, current state, approach, scopes, and the other diagrams) ## Current state (verified on `main`) - `clawsweeper.ts:224,426` - `RealBehaviorProof` records what kind of thing the contributor showed (`status/summary/evidenceKind`), never what ClawSweeper observed. No captured output, no head SHA, no hash, no command field. - `clawsweeper.ts:11130` - the `proof: sufficient` label is written deterministically from the model status. - `apply-result.ts:1104` and `clawsweeper.ts:13612` - two close safety checks trust that label/report via `/^proof:\s*(sufficient|override)\b/i` to decide whether a covering or canonical PR can close another. Automerge itself gates on checks and exact-head review readiness, not this label (`automerge-shepherd.ts:42-82`). - `grep -rn "attest" src/` returns 0. The repair lane already checks out head and runs repo gate commands (`target-validation.ts:230`), so the novelty here is the base-vs-head delta plus a durable attestation record, not first-ever head execution. - `codex-env.ts:67-88` - containment is credential stripping only; there is no egress firewall, and the review lane runs with live network on purpose so it can fetch proof media. ## Motivation Reproduction closes the one unverified link in a system built on evidence over volume: - A pasted proof can be fabricated, stale (captured from an old commit, not the current head), or mock-only that looked live. A re-run cannot be fooled the way a reader can. - For the reproducible subset it removes the model, and its prompt-injection surface, from the close safety decision. The model stays the sole owner of proof for all visual and non-reproducible evidence. - It converts a semantic trust problem (did a model get fooled by hostile words) into an isolation trust problem (can we run untrusted code without leaking creds or reaching the network), a closed and auditable discipline. ## Proposed approach Reproduction is deterministic, not model-driven: run the declared repro on base then head, require old behavior on base and new behavior on head, and decide on exit codes and output hashes only. Captured stdout is attacker-controlled and never flows back into a decision or a model. Flaky or non-differentiating repros go neutral, never green. One honest gap up front: there is no machine-runnable, contributor-declared repro command today. `RealBehaviorProof` has no command field, and `validation_commands` is a repo-level gate, not a per-contributor proof. So this proposes a new optional structured `reproCommand` field (allow-list normalized through the existing `runAllowedValidationCommands` path), and scopes the first stage to cases where either that field is present or the repo's own changed-surface gate is itself the proof (behavior-preserving refactors). Everything else stays human-owned until the field exists. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["PR blocked on proof"] --> B{"evidenceKind reproducible?
terminal / logs / live_output (clawsweeper.ts:231)"} B -->|"no (screenshot, telegram, web_ui_chat)"| H["Leave human/mantis proof queue (clawsweeper.ts:252)"] B -->|"yes"| C{"repro resolvable?
reproCommand OR changed_gate-as-proof"} C -->|"no"| N["verdict: neutral"] C -->|"yes"| S{"netns created?
sudo unshare --net on Blacksmith"} S -->|"no"| N S -->|"yes"| D["De-privileged subprocess, no creds
codexEnv strip + isolateGitHubConfigDir"] D --> E["Run base, base-again, head
capture exit + sha256 hash"] E --> F{"base stable?
base_1 equals base_2"} F -->|"no (flaky)"| N F -->|"yes"| G{"head differs from base?"} G -->|"no"| N G -->|"yes"| K["verdict: attested
write records/[slug]/proof/[n].json + head-pinned comment"] N --> L["No proof: attested label; stays as-is"] K --> M{"gate flag on AND head matches?
(apply-result.ts:1104, default-off)"} M -->|"yes"| P["Prefer attestation over label in close-safety"] M -->|"no / stale head"| Q["Fall back to existing label path"] ``` Example attestation record shape: ```json { "schema_version": 1, "head_sha": "abc123...", "base_sha": "def456...", "repro": { "command": "pnpm vitest run path/to/regression", "source": "repro_command_field" }, "before": { "ref": "base", "exit": 1, "output_hash": "sha256:..." }, "base_stability": { "second_exit": 1, "stable": true }, "after": { "ref": "head", "exit": 0, "output_hash": "sha256:..." }, "differentiates": true, "verdict": "attested" } ``` Example comment shape, posted beside (not replacing) the model verdict: ```markdown Proof reproduction (head abc123): - base def456: FAIL (exit 1) - head abc123: PASS (exit 0) - behavior delta confirmed across the diff Reproduction output withheld (attacker-controlled input; only exit codes and hashes are trusted). Model proof verdict: sufficient. This attestation was produced by re-running the declared reproduction. ``` ## Scopes (staged) 1. Read-only reproduce and attest beside the model verdict. Touches no gate, no dashboard. Mutates nothing. 2. Dashboard surface: show reproduced vs not-reproduced on `/pr-proof-triage`, with fixtures. 3. Gate integration: prefer a valid head-pinned attestation over the model-derived label in the close safety check (`apply-result.ts:1104`), behind a default-off flag. Security-boundary change, maintainer-gated. ```mermaid flowchart TD S1["Scope 1: reproCommand field + reproduce + attest beside verdict
read-only, no gate change
reproduce-proof.ts, proof-attestation.ts, schema/repair"] --> S2["Scope 2: dashboard surface
proof: attested label + view
dashboard/worker.ts + fixture"] S2 --> S3["Scope 3: gate integration
validAttestationForHead preferred over label
apply-result.ts:1104, default-off flag, maintainer-gated"] S1 -. "no mutation risk; lands first" .-> S1 S3 -. "close-safety + containment + schema change; maintainer sign-off" .-> S3 ``` ## Cost Cheap where it counts: reproduction is deterministic runner time, not model tokens, and for the reproducible subset it can remove the high-reasoning proof-judgment call. It runs only on the small set of PRs with a resolvable offline repro, reuses runs the repair lane already performs, rides existing `workers.max`/lane caps, and offsets human proof-triage and bad closes. ## Non-goals - No new close path; reproduction feeds the existing safety checks, it does not create a parallel one. - No auto-green on visual-only proof; screenshots, recordings, and telegram/discord/web-UI-chat proof stay human-owned and are cleanly segregated so the human queue shrinks. - No model in the reproduction decision; the model still advises, deterministic code decides. - No trust of a stale or head-mismatched attestation. - No reliance on a runner firewall that does not exist; egress denial is part of scope, fail-closed if it cannot be established. - No change to the review lane's intentional network access (it needs it to fetch proof media). - No change to the automerge gate, which does not read a proof regex. ## Open questions (called out rather than hidden) - Egress denial runs on Blacksmith self-hosted runners; unprivileged `unshare --net` needs `sudo` or user namespaces and may be constrained by the Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor userns default. Needs a one-line runner probe; the lane fails closed to neutral if a namespace cannot be created. - Adoption is the real gating risk: contributors (or the review model) must supply a `reproCommand`, or the lane only covers changed-surface-is-the-proof cases. - A network-denied sandbox narrows the auto-attestable set to reproducible and offline-deterministic proof, which is smaller than all terminal/logs/live_output; non-deterministic repros (timestamps, temp paths, flaky tests) correctly go neutral. ## Acceptance criteria - A resolvable offline repro where base fails and head passes produces a schema-valid, head-pinned attestation and a marker comment beside the model verdict. - Non-differentiating, flaky-base, timed-out, netns-unavailable, or unresolvable-command cases produce neutral, never a pass. - Raw reproduction output never appears in a decision, a model prompt, or a label; only exit codes and hashes do. - The repro subprocess has no network egress and no GitHub/OpenAI/proof-inspection credentials. - With the flag on, a valid head-matched attestation admits the covering close without a `proof:` label; a stale or absent one falls back to the existing label check with no weakening. - Visual-kind proof paths are unchanged; the dashboard change ships with fixtures. - The sandbox and the label-trusting change carry explicit maintainer review.
Everything that will be done (full implementation dossier) ### Verified receipts | Claim | Location | Verified fact | |---|---|---| | Proof is one model judgment | `clawsweeper.ts:224-230`, `:426-431` | `interface RealBehaviorProof { status; summary; evidenceKind; needsContributorAction }`. No captured output, no SHA, no hash, no command field. | | Judgment parsed as shape only | `clawsweeper.ts:2911-2927` | `parseRealBehaviorProof` = `rejectUnexpectedKeys` + `requireEnum` + `requireString`/`requireBoolean`; content is whatever the model said. | | Model status becomes the label | `clawsweeper.ts:11125-11132` | `nextRealBehaviorProofSufficientLabels`: pushes `PROOF_SUFFICIENT_LABEL` iff `proof.status === "sufficient"`. | | Close-safety checks trust the label/report | `apply-result.ts:1104`; `clawsweeper.ts:13605-13613` | `proofPassedInLabels` (covering-close safety `validatePrCloseCoverageCoveringSafety`) and the canonical-close `unsafeCanonicalPullRequestReason` (`:13615`) both trust `/^proof:\s*(sufficient\|override)\b/i` and/or `reportRealBehaviorProof(...).status`. | | Automerge does NOT gate on proof regex | `automerge-shepherd.ts:42-82` | Gates on merged/state/head-change, `hasTrustedHumanReviewForHead`, `hasTrustedRepairRequestForHead`, `checkBlockReason`, `hasTrustedPassForHead`, mergeable state. No proof-label read. | | No reproduction anywhere | `grep -rn "attest" src/` = 0 | `src/pr-close-coverage-proof.ts` and the config builder `prCloseCoverageProofRuntime` (`apply-result.ts:1443-1479`, `reasoningEffort:"high"`, `timeoutMs:900000`) are distinct model decisions, not re-runs. | | Review prompt fetches attacker media over live network | `clawsweeper.ts:7326-7329` | "You may use the available network and read-only GitHub token to inspect PR body links, comments, screenshots, videos, logs... Download proof artifacts... before inspecting them." Network is intentional (visual-proof inspection). | | Containment today = credential stripping | `codex-env.ts:67-88` | `codexEnv()` deletes `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN`, `CLAWSWEEPER_APP_*`, crabfleet tokens, optionally OpenAI keys. No egress control. | | Validation env does NOT strip the proof token | `target-validation.ts:507-519` | `targetValidationEnv()` strips `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`/`CODEX_*` but not `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN`, `CLAWSWEEPER_APP_*`, or crabfleet tokens. Naive reuse would leak the proof token into an untrusted repro subprocess. | | Repair already runs contributor validation in a checkout | `fix-prompt-builder.ts:245-255`; `target-validation.ts:230-262` | `runAllowedValidationCommands` runs via `runCommand` -> `spawnSync` (`command-runner.ts:24`); no network restriction, full runner network. | | `validation_commands` is a repo-level gate, not a per-contributor repro | `deterministic-automerge-result.ts:63`; `commit-finding-intake.ts:520` | `deterministicAutomergeValidationCommands(repo)` / `validationCommands(repo)` return e.g. `["pnpm check:changed"]`. Repo-canonical, not the contributor's proof. | | Exact-head staleness check exists | `comment-router-core.ts:1053-1066` | `reviewedHeadShaBlockReason({expectedHeadSha, currentHeadSha, markerName})`, reusable verbatim for attestation freshness. | | Head-SHA-keyed durable markers exist | `comment-router-core.ts:2283`; `apply-result.ts:1556` | HTML-comment markers keyed by head SHA, found/updated in place. | | Execution runs on Blacksmith self-hosted | `repair-comment-router.yml`; `repair-cluster-worker.yml` | Worker default `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, execution default `blacksmith-16vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. Review lane uses `ubuntu-latest`. | | No model-free Codex sandbox exec in-repo | `grep -rn "codex debug\|landlock\|seatbelt\|sandbox-exec" src/` = 0 | No evidence ClawSweeper wraps a deterministic command in the Codex sandbox today. | | Mantis proof-only scenarios to segregate | `clawsweeper.ts:252-260` | `MantisRecommendationScenario`; post-#424 the emittable schema enum is telegram/discord/`web_ui_chat_proof` (dropped `slack_desktop_smoke`/`visual_task`). Mantis is now proof-only: reproduce or inspect and return redacted evidence, never mutate. | | Reproducible vs visual evidence kinds | `clawsweeper.ts:231-239` | Reproducible: `terminal`, `logs`, `live_output`. Visual: `screenshot`, `recording`. | | Dashboard proof surface is label-driven | `dashboard/worker.ts:2693,5020,5044,5712` | Views/columns derive from labels via GraphQL search; `proofStateFromLabels` maps labels to a `proof_state` cell. | | Records path convention | `event-record-store.ts:24`; `commit-sweeper.ts:74,69,63` | `records///`; helpers `repoSlug` and `assertSha` (40-hex), currently file-private and duplicated in spirit elsewhere. | ### Security model and residual risk Reproduction runs the declared command on head. That command is arbitrary untrusted code on a Blacksmith self-hosted runner. Two invariants: Invariant 1 - no egress. None exists today. `runAllowedValidationCommands` uses `spawnSync` under `targetValidationEnv()`, which leaves full runner network and does not strip the proof/app/crabfleet tokens (`target-validation.ts:507-519`). A naive reuse would let attacker code exfiltrate `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN` (a live GitHub identity) and reach Blacksmith-internal services. Invariant 2 - captured stdout is attacker-controlled and never re-enters a decision. Only exit codes + output hashes + a recomputed `differentiates` flag may gate. Raw output is stored truncated/redacted for human view only, never fed to a model or a label. Containment primitive (recommended): run the declared repro as a deterministic subprocess (no model), and for egress denial wrap it in a network namespace via `sudo unshare --net` on Blacksmith. - Blacksmith runners grant passwordless `sudo`; `sudo unshare --net -- ` gives the subprocess a loopback-only stack. Plain unprivileged `unshare --net` needs `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, and Ubuntu 24.04 defaults `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, so the `sudo` path (or `unshare --user --map-root-user --net`) is required, not optional. - Inside the namespace, drop back to a de-privileged user before executing untrusted code. - Layer credential stripping: apply `codexEnv()`-style deletion (`codex-env.ts:67-88`, which does strip the proof/app/crabfleet tokens) over `targetValidationEnv()`, plus `scrubGitHubCredentialEnv()` (`commit-sweeper.ts:426`) and `isolateGitHubConfigDir()` (`commit-sweeper.ts:436`). The proof token is used only to check out refs before the sandbox closes and is never present in the repro subprocess env. - Fail-closed: if a network namespace cannot be created (missing sudo, kernel restriction, non-Linux), the lane returns NEUTRAL, never attested. It never falls back to an unconfined run. Residual risk (stated plainly): - `unshare --net` isolates the repro subprocess, not sibling CI steps. A repro that re-execs itself out of the namespace, or a runner image where the netns cannot be created, is a gap - handled by fail-closed NEUTRAL, but it shrinks coverage. - Local CPU/disk abuse remains even with egress denied. Bound by the existing validation timeout (`target-validation.ts:507-525`), lane caps, and a disk-scoped temp checkout. - Attacker-controlled stdout must never gate - only exit code + hash + recomputed delta. - Hash-equality can be gamed by a repro that prints a timestamp (trivially differs base vs head). Mitigation: run base twice; require `base_1 == base_2` (stable) and `head != base`. Any non-determinism -> NEUTRAL. ### Command source decision (load-bearing) There is no structured, machine-runnable contributor reproduction command today. `RealBehaviorProof` has no command field, and `validation_commands` is a repo-level canonical gate (`deterministic-automerge-result.ts:63`, `commit-finding-intake.ts:520`), not a per-contributor proof repro. The lane cannot claim a source that does not exist. So this is an explicit design decision: 1. Add an optional structured field `realBehaviorProof.reproCommand` (string, nullable), populated by the review model and/or the contributor, allow-list-normalized through `runAllowedValidationCommands` (`target-validation.ts:230`) before execution. Extends the strict parser (`clawsweeper.ts:2911`) with one `requireNullableString` field and a schema-version bump. 2. Stage 1 engages only when a reproduction actually exists: the repo's canonical `changed_gate` is the proof (behavior-preserving refactors, where "run the changed-surface gate on base vs head" is a meaningful delta), or a `reproCommand` is present on the report. Everything else stays human-owned until the field is populated. Adoption of `reproCommand`, not execution, is the real gating risk. ### Design Reproduction engine (`src/repair/reproduce-proof.ts`, new): - Inputs: repo, PR number, `base_sha`, `head_sha`, resolved repro command (from `reproCommand` or the repo `changed_gate`). - Checkout: temp worktree mirroring the `local-range--` pattern (`clawsweeper.ts:6885`), clean-tree enforced via `dirtyWorktree()` (`commit-sweeper.ts:420`). - Execution (in the netns sandbox, no model): checkout base -> run (before), run again (base stability), checkout head -> run (after). Capture needs a non-throwing spawn returning `{status, stdout, stderr}` - note `runCommand` throws on non-zero and returns stdout only (`command-runner.ts:14-48`), so the engine adds a thin `spawnSync`-based wrapper (the exit code is the signal). - Outputs per run: `exit`, `output_hash` (sha256 over stdout+stderr), `output_bytes`, `duration_ms`. - Verdict (fail-closed): `attested` iff `base_1 == base_2` (stable) and head differs from base (exit or hash). Otherwise `neutral`: flaky base, no delta, timeout, netns-unavailable, or unresolvable command. Attestation schema + writer (`src/repair/proof-attestation.ts`, new): schema at `schema/repair/clawsweeper-proof-attestation.schema.json`. Record path `records//proof/.json` via `repoSlug()`/`assertSha()` - lift these to one canonical home rather than re-duplicate. ```json { "schema_version": 1, "repo": "openclaw/openclaw", "number": 12345, "head_sha": "<40-hex>", "base_sha": "<40-hex>", "repro": { "command": "pnpm check:changed", "source": "repro_command|changed_gate", "cwd": "." }, "before": { "ref": "base", "exit": 1, "output_hash": "sha256:...", "output_bytes": 812, "duration_ms": 4200 }, "base_stability": { "second_exit": 1, "second_output_hash": "sha256:...", "stable": true }, "after": { "ref": "head", "exit": 0, "output_hash": "sha256:...", "output_bytes": 640, "duration_ms": 4310 }, "differentiates": true, "verdict": "attested", "reason": "base stable (exit 1 twice); head exit 0 differs", "runner_id": "blacksmith-16vcpu-...", "engine": "reproduce-attest", "engine_version": 1, "attested_at": "2026-07-05T00:00:00Z" } ``` `parseProofAttestation` reuses the strict style (`requireRecord` + `rejectUnexpectedKeys` + `requireEnum` + `requireString`/`requireInteger`/`requireBoolean`, cf. `clawsweeper.ts:2505-2549,2911`). `differentiates`/`verdict` are recomputed by the reader from `before`/`after`/`base_stability`, never trusted from disk (VISION 7, fail-closed). Comment (beside the model verdict): marker ``, following the head-SHA-keyed convention (`comment-router-core.ts:2283`). Body: repro command, base/head exit codes, `differentiates`, and an explicit note that reproduction output is withheld. Never renders raw output. Freshness enforced at read time via `reviewedHeadShaBlockReason(...)` (`comment-router-core.ts:1053`). Dashboard surface: `dashboard/worker.ts` is label-driven. Add a `proof: attested` label written by the lane, then: add it to `PR_PROOF_LABEL_NAMES`; extend `proofStateFromLabels` (`:2693`) to return "Attested (reproduced)" above "Sufficient"; add a `PR_PROOF_VIEWS` entry and a metric tile. The existing `proof` column (`proofStateCell` `:5712`) renders it unchanged. Fixture in `test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` (required schema/label proof, VISION line 148). Gate integration (narrow, staged, fail-closed): at `apply-result.ts:1104`, inside `validatePrCloseCoverageCoveringSafety` (which already fetches the covering pull request at `:1095`; head SHA available as `pullRequest.head?.sha`): ``` const proofPassed = validAttestationForHead(result.repo, coveringRef, pullRequest.head?.sha) || labels.some((label) => /^proof:\s*(sufficient|override)\b/i.test(label)); ``` `validAttestationForHead` reads the record, re-validates schema, recomputes `differentiates`, and calls `reviewedHeadShaBlockReason`. Returns `true` only if `verdict==="attested"` and head matches. Any error/absent/stale/neutral -> `false` (existing label path). Gated behind `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_ATTESTATION_GATE=1`, default off. The canonical-close sibling (`clawsweeper.ts:13611`) is a later, separate follow-up. This prefers an attestation over the label; it never weakens the current check when absent. ### Tiering - Auto-attest lane engages only when `evidenceKind` is reproducible (`terminal`, `logs`, `live_output`, `clawsweeper.ts:231-239`) and a repro exists (`reproCommand` or `changed_gate`-as-proof) and the repro is offline-deterministic. - Stays human-owned: `screenshot`, `recording`, and every Mantis proof-only case (`clawsweeper.ts:252-260`; post-#424 telegram/discord/`web_ui_chat_proof`). The lane no-ops on these; the mantis/human proof queue is untouched. Net effect: the human proof queue loses only the reproducible-and-offline-deterministic cases; visual paths do not change. ### Staged scopes mapped to files (three scopes) | Scope | What lands | Files | |---|---|---| | 1. Reproduce + attest beside the verdict (read-only) | `reproCommand` field + reproduction engine + attestation writer + marker comment. No gate change. | `src/repair/reproduce-proof.ts` (new), `src/repair/proof-attestation.ts` (new), `schema/repair/clawsweeper-proof-attestation.schema.json` (new), `clawsweeper.ts:2911` (add optional field), review path wiring; reuse `commit-sweeper.ts:420/426/436`, `target-validation.ts:230/507`, `codex-env.ts:67`, `comment-router-core.ts:1053/2283`. | | 2. Dashboard surface | `proof: attested` label, `proofStateFromLabels`, view + metric. | `dashboard/worker.ts:2693,5020,5044` + `PR_PROOF_LABEL_NAMES`/`PR_PROOF_VIEWS`; fixture in `test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`. | | 3. Gate integration | `validAttestationForHead` preferred over the label, default-off flag. | `src/repair/apply-result.ts:1104` + `src/repair/proof-attestation.ts`. | The v1 "standalone network-default fix" is dropped as a fix: the review lane's CI network is intentional for media fetch (`clawsweeper.ts:7326-7329`), so `codexReviewNetworkAccess=false` never firing (it is only emitted for `workspace-write`, `execute-fix-artifact.ts:2686`, while CI review runs `danger-full-access`, `:227`) is by design, not a bug to flip. ### Tests and fixtures (comment-free, per repo rule) 1. Reproduce -> attestation: base fails, head passes -> `verdict:"attested"`, `differentiates:true`, schema-valid. 2. Non-differentiating -> neutral: identical exit+hash -> `neutral`, no label. 3. Flaky base -> neutral: `base_1 != base_2` -> `neutral`. 4. Netns-unavailable -> neutral: sandbox creation fails -> `neutral`, never unconfined run. 5.
